title: Private Dedicated Pool — sync jot and follow-ups
body:
Meeting context / goal:
- Prep notes for sync with SRE + Solutions (weekly 1:1 follow-up). Primary objective: decide reservation sizing for Q3 trial customers on private dedicated pools and lock autoscale cooldown defaults.
- Secondary: capture short-term mitigation for network egress throttling observed in last canary.

Agenda (15–20m):
1) Quick status (2m): current pool count, hot vs cold nodes.
2) Telemetry highlights (3m): utilization, queue depth, tail latency.
3) Reservation proposal (6m): sizing options + cost tradeoffs.
4) Autoscale policy defaults (4m): warm pools, cooldowns, burst cap.
5) Action items & owners (3–5m).

Current snapshot (notes from dashboards, pulled 2025-06-09):
- Total private pools in org: 6 (region: eu-west1 x2, us-central1 x3, ap-southeast1 x1).
- Provisioned GPUs (sum): 72 A100s equivalent (mixed 80/40/20 configs).
- 7-day avg utilization: 58% (peak window 11:00–15:00 UTC shows 78%).
- Median queue wait: 120ms; 99th percentile queue wait: 1.1s on heavy prompt-days.
- Observed cold-start penalty: first-token tail adds ~220ms when cold worker must pull weights (not using shared KV cache).

Assumptions for Q3 trial sizing (base numbers for discussion):
- Expected incremental client demand: +18% token throughput month-over-month for first 3 months after onboarding.
- SLA target for trial customers: p95 latency <= 600ms for standard completions, p99 <= 1.2s.
- Budget constraint: increase monthly committed spend by <= 25% relative to current private spend baseline.

Quick back-of-envelope reservation scenarios:
Option A — conservative (aim for 65% avg util):
- Target provisioned GPUs: 80 -> additional +8 (from 72).
- Expected headroom for bursts: ~12 GPUs.
- Est. committed monthly delta: +24% (within budget).

Option B — aggressive (aim for 75% avg util with burst tolerant):
- Target provisioned GPUs: 92 -> +20 (from 72).
- Expected sustained throughput improvement but higher idle hours off-peak.
- Est. committed monthly delta: +48% (exceeds stated budget unless negotiated pricing).

Option C — hybrid w/ autoscale + buffer (recommended interim):
- Reserve a baseline of 78 GPUs (+6) and keep a 12-GPU burst pool (on-demand or short-term reserved).
- Configure autoscale to add burst nodes with pre-warm images (reduce cold penalty).
- Estimated cost delta: +30% committed + on-demand bursts billed separately.

Tradeoffs / risks to call out quickly:
- Over-reserving ties capital and increases unit cost off-peak.
- Under-reserve increases p99 queue waits and will hurt trial experience.
- Network egress bottleneck: one eu-west1 pool showed 18% packet drops chasing a misconfigured firewall rule in canary — must patch before increasing reservation in that region.
- KMS integration for private pools: rollout of new key rotation may require short restart window (impact estimation: 10–20min per node) — schedule outside peak.

Autoscale policy draft (defaults to propose):
- Scale up trigger: queue depth > 0.45 * active_workers for 30s OR avg token rate per worker > 0.85 capacity for 60s.
- Scale down trigger: sustained avg utilization < 0.4 for 5m and queue depth == 0 for 2m.
- Cooldown: 3m after scale-up before allowing scale-down; 4m after scale-down before next scale-up attempt.
- Pre-warm behaviour: keep golden AMI image and cached model shard on a warm pool; when burst requested, start from warm image to shave ~150–200ms from cold-start.
- Burst cap: cap on-demand burst to 20% of baseline reservation to control cost.

Operational checklist before increasing reservation in eu-west1:
- [ ] Fix firewall rule (Jorge) — remove restrictive egress NAT for model shard downloads. Target: 2025-06-13.
- [ ] Run 2x canary cycles with patched images (Priya) — confirm no packet loss. Target: 2025-06-16.
- [ ] Validate KMS key rotation impact in staging (Liam) — schedule test 2025-06-12.
- [ ] Update customer-facing runbook (Maya) — include expected restart windows and SLA caveats. Target: 2025-06-17.

Follow-ups (assignments & due dates):
- Jorge A.: firewall fix + post-fix telemetry check (2025-06-13).
- Priya D.: run canary cycles, capture p99 queue wait numbers and packet loss (2025-06-16).
- Liam O.: KMS rotation dry-run in staging, document restart behavior (2025-06-12).
- Maya C.: draft reservation justification email + cost delta spreadsheet to finance & solutions (2025-06-14).
- SRE lead (TBD): approve autoscale cooldown defaults and add to cluster configuration (2025-06-18).

Questions to raise in the sync (short bullets to ask SRE/product):
- Can we get a guaranteed on-demand burst discount if we commit to a baseline + burst contract (ask sales/finance to model)?
- Any objections to 3m cooldown? operationally sensible or too aggressive?
- Do we have automated warm image builders for private pools, or do we need a short engineering spike to bake warm AMIs?
- Are any legal/compliance concerns around increased network egress for multi-region shard syncs?

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep wording simple when emailing finance — show two clear scenarios (C conservative, H hybrid recommended) and one concrete ask (approve +6 GPUs baseline + allow on-demand bursts up to 12).
- Capture historical 2025-04 spike events as appendix in the email — shows why pure autoscale only is risky for first 30 days of trial.
- Make sure to reference INF-1823 in the reservation request to speed up approvals.

Small calculations pasted for quick sanity check:
- Current avg tokens/hr per GPU = 1.1M tokens (org metric) -> with 72 GPUs = ~79.2M tokens/hr. +18% growth -> need ~93.5M tokens/hr -> equivalent GPUs at same efficiency = 85 GPUs -> suggests baseline ~85 if growth realized.
- Buffer math: target baseline = ceil(85 * 0.92) -> 78 (rounded) -> aligns with hybrid plan baseline 78.

Appendix / artifacts to attach to email (links):
- CONFLUENCE:private-deploy-runbook-456 (current runbook)
- JIRA INF-1823 (reservation ticket)
- small csv export of the last 14 days utilization (attached when sending)

End notes: keep this doc light — convert to a short decision memo after the sync with the chosen option and send to finance & sales.

Timestamp: 2025-06-10 09:12 (UTC) — Maya C.
